what_this_run_supports: The accepted OUTCOME A result is independently reproduced and is NOT retracted. Under the frozen geometry rule (sha256 a7452748d40c511a14a1c7848ece5fe7f8f8901cc30f45a66918c89eb593a633, re-hashed identically from three independent sources) applied to the served bundles of gate_packet/38839347028 (de 214, fr 217, it 211 decisions, all three sha256 re-verified), relevance_ordered passes 22/33 criteria against the incumbent's 16/33, with ZERO regressions on any bundle (de 7/11, fr 8/11, it 7/11 versus 6/5/5). hydrate_then_cluster passes 20/33 and regresses on OUTLIER_VALIDITY on de and fr.

The incumbent reproduction lands exactly on the accepted verdict of record (ACCEPTED_frontier-served-packet-falsification_38880639079.json, pass_counts de 6 / fr 5 / it 5, baselines 5/5/4, french_largest_share 0.7696). All 99 criterion verdicts computed by the auditor agree with the committed artifacts, degenerate flags included.

The cycle's headline finding is TRUE and verified at source: the variants emit unique negative cluster_ids for un-hydrated shells, and product/static/query.html:188 computes ctx.fillStyle=COLORS[(p.cluster_id??0)%COLORS.length] against an 8-entry palette (:141). JavaScript % truncates toward zero, so a negative id yields a negative index, COLORS[negative] is undefined, and the canvas ignores an invalid fillStyle and keeps the previous point's colour. Independently confirmed: the negative-id set is exactly the un-hydrated shell set (detail_status != search_hit), 47/49/47 rows, with the additive unclustered flag set on exactly those rows; every emitted cluster record has a non-negative id, so the legend (:240) is unaffected.

This is an ADOPTION-TIME hazard, not a live production bug: the shipped geometry derives cluster ids from sklearn labels and nearest-centroid assignment (product/query/qmap.py:353-390) and never emits a negative id. The team's characterisation and its refusal to fix rendering code or to work around the id on the variant side are both correct under the charter.

The vendored scorer's byte-identity is now PROVEN rather than asserted, and the auditor confirmed it independently: metrics.py blob 3fc32b5562a612fa1afc7e91a50960f21dcba168 and textgeo.py blob 425e70face1fb1549e20e3075640b076c2134831 are identical in the team's vendored copy and in evaluation/frozen_bars/vendored/frontier_map_semantics_reference on origin/lab/evaluation.

The component is a pure, deterministic function of the bundle behind the query_result_bundle seam: no rendering, UI, colour or interaction file is touched, relations[] is untouched, every row keeps source_url/canonical_url and decision_id, no decision is dropped or duplicated, member_ids stays capped at 50 with size as true membership, and per-bundle geometry cost is 0.05-0.17 s against the frozen 2.0 s budget.

gate_rationale.why_not_pass: A material, claim-bearing field of the accepted INTEGRATION_CONTRACT.json is false (the [-1,1] coordinate guarantee) and the cycle that declared itself an adoption-readiness audit amended drop_in_path but not this. Passing would integrate a component whose delivered contract advertises a guarantee it does not meet, against a product lane that documents and enforces the opposite convention.
gate_rationale.why_not_revise: REVISE mechanically re-dispatches frontier-team.yml with repair_round+1, manufacturing a THIRD dispatch of a charter whose stop_promote_rule says 'never re-dispatch it with the same charter_version', bypassing the supervisor guard entirely and guaranteeing another audit cycle of this same kind. The defects are addressed to Core Product and frontier-query-map-ui, not to another producer cycle.
gate_rationale.why_blocked: Two independent reasons. (1) Recurring pathology must become BLOCKED rather than infinite REVISE: this is the third dispatch of a closed charter and the pathology has already survived one prose escalation. (2) BLOCKED is the only gate value that writes state/blockers/frontier/<team>.json, which the supervisor tests with a LOCAL FILE TEST rather than the fail-open 'gh api contents ... || true' pipeline that let two consecutive dispatches through despite correct, unchanged data on the lab branch. From that point the supervisor prints 'blocked under current charter; Director must redirect/kill/recharter it' and sets NEED_DIRECTOR, which is the correct resting state for a finished charter carrying two lane-owned adoption preconditions.
gate_rationale.what_blocked_does_not_do: It does not un-publish this cycle's delta: the producer works directly on lab/frontier/<team> by workflow design, so dc3ffc6 is already the lab branch head whatever the gate says. It does not retract OUTCOME A, the 22/33 result, or the team's renderer finding, all of which are verified and stand. It does not discard the evidence: the team's own artifacts are on the lab branch and this audit report lands on cycle/frontier/frontier-query-conditioned-map-geometry/38978981369/audit, referenced by blocked_by_run.
gate_rationale.fairness_note: The producer was honest, added real verified value, and broke no charter rule. BLOCKED here is an instrument choice, not a judgement of the work: the recommendation to the Director is to ADOPT relevance_ordered after RF1-RF4, not to discard it.
